claims.statement: Flux uses the dependsOn field to create installation order across Kustomizations, such as cilium-gateway depending on cert-manager, and cluster-apps depending on CRD Kustomizations.

Application Kustomizations follow a standard pattern with commonMetadata.labels for app identification, decryption via sops-age, postBuild substitution from cluster-secrets, prune enabled for garbage collection, and wait enabled for health assurance.

SOPS encryption rules for Kubernetes secrets encrypt only data and stringData fields (encrypted_regex), use mac_only_encrypted to preserve YAML structure, and apply to (bootstrap|kubernetes)/.*\.sops\.ya?ml files with the cluster's age recipient.
Flux Kustomizations use standard reconciliation intervals of 1 hour with 2-minute retry intervals, 5-minute timeouts, and wait enabled to ensure resources are healthy before marking ready.

The bjw-s-labs app-template Helm chart is vendored once as a shared OCIRepository (currently pinned to ref.tag 5.2.1, with a Helm-chart layerSelector) inside the `common` Kustomize component that every app namespace includes; application HelmReleases consume it via chartRef kind OCIRepository name app-template, so chart upgrades are a single tag bump.

The reusable `image-automation` Kustomize component adds three per-app resources — an ExternalSecret for registry credentials from Bitwarden, an ImageRepository scanning every 1m, and an ImagePolicy labeled `image-automation: enabled` that selects the newest timestamp from tags matching `^.+-[a-f0-9]+-(?P<ts>[0-9]+)$` — all parameterized through postBuild substitution variables (APP, NAMESPACE, REGISTRY_URL).

A single cluster-wide ImageUpdateAutomation runs every 5 minutes with the Setters strategy scoped to ./kubernetes/apps/default, commits as flux-bot to main of the flux-system-https GitRepository, and its policySelector (matchLabels image-automation: enabled) restricts updates to ImagePolicies created by the image-automation component; apps consume the resolved tag via the `{"$imagepolicy": "NAMESPACE:APP:tag"}` setter marker in HelmRelease values.

dependsOn is declared per Kustomization (not per app directory), enabling cross-namespace ordering such as gitea waiting on topolvm, external-secrets, and cloudnative-pg-cluster while its sibling gitea-runner repeats only storage and external-secrets; HelmReleases additionally self-heal with install/upgrade remediation (retries, rollback, cleanupOnFail).

Upstream CRDs are delivered from the upstream repos via pinned GitRepositories in kubernetes/flux/meta/repos: external-dns-crds points at https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/external-dns (Renovate-managed tag v0.23.0, interval 15m, ignore restricted to /config/crd/standard/) and gateway-api at https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api (tag v1.6.2, interval 15m, ignore restricted to /config/crd/experimental/); both are wired into the repos kustomization and back the external-dns-crds and gateway-api-crds Kustomizations in kubernetes/flux/cluster/ks.yaml, which cluster-apps depends on.

The flux-instance HelmRelease values configure Flux's sync to point at the GitRepository for github.com/tomyail/talos-cluster.git refs/heads/main with path kubernetes/flux/cluster, which is what applies the root Kustomizations from kubernetes/flux/cluster/ks.yaml; the distribution version 2.9.5 is Renovate-pinned and all six Flux controllers are enabled.

Flux is installed via GitOps rather than flux bootstrap: the flux-operator Kustomization deploys the ControlPlane Flux operator with a healthCheck on its own HelmRelease, and the flux-instance Kustomization (dependsOn flux-operator) deploys the pinned flux-instance OCI chart with install remediation retries -1 and upgrade rollback with 3 retries.

kubernetes/flux/cluster/ks.yaml defines four root Kustomizations in flux-system: cluster-meta (path ./kubernetes/flux/meta, no dependencies), gateway-api-crds and external-dns-crds (each dependsOn cluster-meta, 5m timeout), and cluster-apps (path ./kubernetes/apps, dependsOn cluster-meta plus both CRD Kustomizations), so no application reconciles until the upstream CRDs and source repositories exist.

cluster-meta reconciles kubernetes/flux/meta, which contains the repos/ directory registering roughly thirty upstream GitRepository chart sources (cilium, cloudnative-pg, grafana, jetstack, etc.) that application HelmReleases depend on; cluster-meta also hardcodes targetNamespace flux-system for Renovate lookups.

Gateway API and external-dns CRDs are pulled from upstream release tags via pinned GitRepositories (gateway-api v1.6.2 from kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api, external-dns-crds v0.23.0 from kubernetes-sigs/external-dns), each with a 15m interval and an ignore block exposing only /config/crd/experimental/ or /config/crd/standard/; Renovate manages the tags, and bootstrap-apps.sh also applies these CRDs directly during first bootstrap.

All root and flux-system Kustomizations decrypt SOPS files with decryption provider sops referencing the sops-age Secret, which holds an age private key encrypted for recipient age1shkd7fsr...; the secret is seeded out-of-band into flux-system by scripts/bootstrap-apps.sh before Flux can reconcile, and re-applied thereafter through the common Kustomize component.

Application and flux-system Kustomizations use postBuild.substituteFrom with the cluster-secrets Secret (SOPS-encrypted, seeded by bootstrap-apps.sh, shipped in the common component) so ${VAR} placeholders like SECRET_DOMAIN and TIMEZONE are replaced cluster-wide, with per-app variables added via inline postBuild.substitute entries.

Root Kustomizations uniformly set prune: true (garbage-collect resources deleted from Git), retryInterval: 2m (fast retry of failed reconciles), wait: true (health-wait resources before Ready, with --requeue-dependency=5s making dependency checks quick), interval: 1h steady state (shortened by the GitHub Receiver webhook), and timeout: 5m on CRD and cluster-apps reconciles.

The flux-instance Kustomization also ships a GitHub notification Receiver (events ping/push) targeting the flux-system GitRepository, authenticated by a SOPS-encrypted github-webhook-token-secret, so pushes trigger immediate reconciliation instead of waiting for the poll interval.

App Kustomizations declare dependsOn edges to infrastructure they need; gitea depends on topolvm (storage), external-secrets, and cloudnative-pg-cluster (database), and its companion gitea-runner Kustomization depends on topolvm and external-secrets.

App Kustomizations inject environment config via postBuild.substituteFrom cluster-secrets and per-app inline postBuild.substitute variables; gitea sets APP (anchored to its name and commonMetadata labels) and VOLSYNC_CAPACITY: 10Gi, and Kustomize components such as components/volsync-new and components/gatus/external inherit the substitution.

Reconciliation ordering between Flux Kustomizations is expressed only through dependsOn; listing order in a namespace kustomization.yaml changes only build output order, so gating or reordering an app requires editing dependsOn, and a new app needing an upstream chart must register that source under kubernetes/flux/meta/repos (reconciled by cluster-meta) before cluster-apps builds it.

Root and app Kustomizations uniformly set prune: true (garbage-collect resources removed from Git), wait: true (health-wait created resources; dependents stay DependenciesNotReady, re-checked every 5s via --requeue-dependency), retryInterval: 2m, interval: 1h, and timeout: 5m on slow API-heavy Kustomizations.

The root hierarchy in kubernetes/flux/cluster/ks.yaml is cluster-meta (kubernetes/flux/meta, GitRepository flux-system), gateway-api-crds (config/crd/experimental from the pinned kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api GitRepository) and external-dns-crds (config/crd/standard from kubernetes-sigs/external-dns) both depending on cluster-meta, and cluster-apps (kubernetes/apps) depending on all three; the two CRD GitRepositories use ignore scoping so only the CRD directories are served.

Cluster changes flow through a commit→reconcile loop: source-controller polls the flux-system GitRepository and snapshots commits as artifacts; the GitHub Receiver (with its SOPS-encrypted webhook token) triggers immediate reconciliation on push instead of waiting for the poll; and `task reconcile` in Taskfile.yaml manually forces this via `flux reconcile kustomization flux-system --with-source`, with preconditions on the repo-local kubeconfig and the flux binary.

Reconciliation is pausable per object via `spec.suspend: true` on Kustomization/HelmRelease objects; the namespace-root Kustomizations explicitly pin `suspend: false` (e.g. kubernetes/apps/database/namespace.yaml and kubernetes/apps/storage/namespace.yaml), so namespaces are re-enabled by Git commit alone.

Self-built images are updated by Flux image automation, not Renovate: the components/image-automation component (spliced into app ks.yaml files such as fava) provides an ExternalSecret for registry credentials, an ImageRepository scanning tags every 1m, and an ImagePolicy selecting the newest `-.+-[a-f0-9]+-<ts>` tag; the app HelmRelease image tag carries a `$imagepolicy` setter comment that image-automation-controller rewrites.

Two ImageUpdateAutomation objects (kubernetes/apps/flux-system/image-automation/automation.yaml covering ./kubernetes/apps/default and a fava-scoped one) run every 5m with the Setters strategy, check out main via the flux-system-https GitRepository (HTTPS clone authenticated by flux-github-token), and push tag updates as flux-bot commits directly to main — closing the loop back into reconciliation; only policies labeled image-automation: enabled are selected.

Renovate runs on a weekend schedule, ignores **/*.sops.* files, and groups updates (including a 'Flux Operator' group matching flux-operator/flux-instance), delivering upgrades of pinned tags and chart/distribution versions as PRs.
